## CloudflareApi

Cloudflare’s operationIds are machine artifacts (`zones-get` vs
`zones-0-get` — the `-0-` is a generator’s dedup counter), so rather
than cleaning them up we name every op mechanically from its verb and
path: the group is the path’s non-parameter segments, nested
(`zones.dns_records`), and the method is the HTTP verb — except that
when a group has both a collection GET and a single-item GET they become
`list` and `get`. Two fixups keep the whole surface collision-free:
sibling paths differing only by an interior parameter gain a
`_by_<param>` suffix, and an action segment that would shadow an op
folds into its parent as `<segment>_<verb>`. So `GET /zones` is
`zones.list`, `GET /zones/{zone_id}` is `zones.get`, and
`GET /user/tokens/verify` is `user.tokens.verify.get` — a user who knows
the URL knows the call.

*A fastspec `group_func` looking up precomputed `names` by canonical

The parsed surface ships with the package as `cf_spec.py`, fastspec’s
compact form (`SpecParser.save`): 2.6MB instead of the 8MB raw schema,
loaded in ~30ms instead of a ~0.3s parse, with the naming machinery
above running only at regeneration time.
[`build_spec`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcflare/core.html#build_spec)
refreshes it from Cloudflare’s published schema; op names can shift when
the spec changes, so review that diff before shipping it.

The naming is only trustworthy if it can never silently collide —
`OpGroup` exposes ops with `setattr`, so a duplicate name would shadow
its sibling (exactly the bug this design replaces). This walk asserts
the built tree is clean: within every group, op names are unique
(duplicates allowed only for the same endpoint spelled two ways in the
spec) and no op shares a name with a subgroup.

``` python
def _surface_ok(g):
    nms = [o.name for o in g.ops]
    for n,c in Counter(nms).items():
        if c>1: assert len({tuple(snake(s) for s in o.op_spec.path.strip('/').split('/')) for o in g.ops if o.name==n})==1, f'dup op {g.name}.{n}'
    assert not set(nms)&set(g.subgroups), f'op/subgroup shadow in {g.name}: {set(nms)&set(g.subgroups)}'
    for sg in g.subgroups.values(): _surface_ok(sg)

for grp in cli.groups.values(): _surface_ok(grp)
len(cli.groups), len(cli.groups['zones'].subgroups)
```

    (15, 60)

### CloudflareApi

``` python
def CloudflareApi(
    token:NoneType=None, # API token; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` when `api_key` and `email` aren't given
    account_id:NoneType=None, # Account ID; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
    email:NoneType=None, # Account email for a global API key; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL`
    api_key:NoneType=None, # Global API key; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY` when no token is given or set
    account_token:bool=False, # Is `token` an account-owned token (uses `/accounts/{account_id}/tokens/verify`)?
):
```

*Cloudflare API client supporting user tokens, account tokens, and
global API keys*

ucf = CloudflareApi()
(await ucf.verify()).result.status

``` python

    grp:str='account.zone.', # Resource prefix after `com.cloudflare.api.`
    account_token:bool=False, # Create an account-owned token (nests zone resources under `account_id`)?
    account_id:str=None, # Account ID for account-owned tokens; defaults to `self.account_id`
):
```

## R2 tokens and S3 credentials

Cloudflare R2 S3 credentials derive directly from an R2 API token:
`access_key_id` is the token ID and `secret_access_key` is the SHA-256
hex digest of the token value. `create_r2_token` creates either an
account-owned service token (default) or a user token, scoped to
specific buckets or the whole account, and returns both the API response
and derived S3 credentials.

### r2_s3_creds

``` python
def r2_s3_creds(
    token_id:str, # Cloudflare API token ID (becomes `access_key_id`)
    token_value:str, # Cloudflare API token secret value (SHA-256 hex becomes `secret_access_key`)
    account_id:str=None, # Account ID; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
    jurisdiction:str='default', # R2 jurisdiction (`'default'`, `'eu'`, `'fedramp'`)
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Derive S3-compatible R2 credentials (`access_key_id`,
`secret_access_key`, `endpoint`, `region`) from a Cloudflare R2 API
token.*

[`r2_s3_creds`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcflare/core.html#r2_s3_creds)
derives S3 credentials offline from any existing token pair:

``` python
creds = r2_s3_creds('tok-id', 'tok-val', account_id='acct123')
assert len(creds.secret_access_key) == 64 and creds.endpoint == 'https://acct123.r2.cloudflarestorage.com'
creds.endpoint, creds.region
```

### CloudflareApi.create_r2_token

``` python
async def create_r2_token(
    name:str, # Name for the new R2 token
    buckets:NoneType=None, # Bucket name or iterable of bucket names; None grants account-wide R2 access
    write:bool=True, # Grant read/write access (False for read-only)
    account_id:str=None, # Account ID; defaults to `self.account_id`
    account_token:bool=True, # Create an account-owned service token (False for a user-owned token)
    jurisdiction:str='default', # R2 jurisdiction for bucket-scoped resources (`'default'`, `'eu'`, `'fedramp'`)
    expires_on:str=None, # Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Create a Cloudflare R2 API token and return both the API response
(`token`) and derived S3 credentials (`s3`).*

Global API key authentication fills `email` and `account_id` from
`CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`:

``` python
if api_key and email and acctid:
    gcf = CloudflareApi(api_key=api_key)
    assert (await gcf.verify()).success
```

``` python
if api_key and email and acctid:
    r2 = await gcf.create_r2_token('fastcflare-r2-test-token', buckets='fastcflare-test-bucket', write=False)
    try:
        assert r2.token.success and len(r2.s3.secret_access_key) == 64
        r2_cf = CloudflareApi(token=r2.token.result.value, account_token=True)
        assert (await r2_cf.verify()).result.status == 'active'
    finally: assert (await gcf.accounts.tokens.delete(acctid, r2.token.result.id)).success
    r2.s3.endpoint, r2.s3.region
```
